Chapter 04

TypeScript, tightened

Two extra compiler flags that catch real crashes, and the one setting SvelteKit 3 now requires you to write yourself.

By the end of this chapter

Your tsconfig.json is stricter than the default and pnpm run check passes.

Open tsconfig.json. The scaffold gives you something short, because most of the configuration comes from a file SvelteKit generates:

strict: true is doing a lot of work — it turns on strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny and half a dozen others. We're going to add three more, and one required section.

noUncheckedIndexedAccess is the one that matters

Without it, TypeScript claims array[0] is definitely a T. It is not — the array might be empty. With the flag on, you get T | undefined and have to deal with it. It is mildly irritating for about a day and then it starts catching real "cannot read properties of undefined" crashes before they ship.

The include and exclude arrays are not optional in SvelteKit 3. The generated config no longer guesses them. Leave them out and svelte-check will happily type-check your minified production build in build/ and report a couple of thousand meaningless errors — which is a genuinely bewildering first experience.

Checking your work

TypeScript on its own does not understand .svelte files. svelte-check does — it type-checks your components, your markup expressions and your props:

Run this constantly. It is the fastest feedback loop in the project, and unlike the dev server it checks files you are not currently looking at.

Checkpoint

pnpm run check prints 0 errors. If it reports thousands, you have not added the exclude array.
